title: Mariana's Spain (from Tubal), Sammes's Phoenician Britain, Strutt & Bede's Heptarchy, Mézeray's France & Sandford's Portugal

nodes.name: Mariana's General History of Spain (1699 Book I Ch. I): Tubal (5th Son of Japheth, 131 yrs after Flood) → Ancient Kings of Spain
nodes.era: Post-Flood Dispersion (Mariana 1699 Book I Ch. I p. 1)
nodes.role: Spaniards Traced Directly from Tubal, 5th Son of Japheth
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (tr. Stevens 1699) Book I Ch. I p. 1
nodes.notes: Mariana opens his monumental history of Spain (p. 1): 'Tubal, the son of Japheth, was the first man that peopled Spain after the Flood... the 5th son of Japheth, was sent to the farthest regions westward, that is, to Spain, where he founded the Spanish monarchy.'

nodes.name: Visigothic Kingdom of Spain (Mariana 1699): Ataulf → Leovigild → King Reccared I (589 CE) → King Roderick (711 CE)
nodes.role: Gothic Sovereigns of Hispania Bridged to Islamic Al-Andalus
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Traces Visigothic Hispania from Alaric's successor Ataulf and Toledo unifier Leovigild to King Reccared I (589 CE) and last Visigothic king Roderick (711 CE).

nodes.name: Reconquista Spain (Mariana 1699): Don Pelayo of Asturias (718) → Alfonso VI of Castile & Leon → Ferdinand III & James I of Aragon
nodes.role: Asturian, Castilian, Leonese & Aragonese Christian Crowns
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Follows the Christian continuity from Don Pelayo at Covadonga (718 CE) through Alfonso VI of Castile and Leon (father-in-law of Count Henry of Burgundy/Portugal), St. Ferdinand III, and James I the Conqueror of Aragon.

nodes.name: Unified Catholic & Habsburg Spain (Mariana 1699): Ferdinand of Aragon & Isabella of Castile (1492) → Emperor Charles V → King Philip II
nodes.role: Unifiers of Aragon & Castile and Spanish Habsburg Dynasty
sources: Juan de Mariana The General History of Spain (1699)
nodes.notes: Unites Castile and Aragon under Ferdinand II and Isabella I (1492), continuing through Joanna the Mad and Philip the Handsome to Emperor Charles V (Charles I of Spain) and King Philip II.

nodes.name: Aylett Sammes's Phoenician Britain (1676): Tyre & Sidon Tin Trade ('Bratanac') + Cimmerian / Gomerite Britons
nodes.role: Phoenician & Cimmerian-Gomerite Origin of Ancient Britain
sources: Aylett Sammes Antiquities of Ancient Britain (1676) p. 2
nodes.notes: Sammes rejects later fables in favor of classical Phoenician sources, arguing that Phoenician navigators from Sidon and Tyre ('Barat-anac' / land of tin) discovered and settled Britain alongside Gomerite Cimmerian peoples.

nodes.name: Ancient British Kings vs. Rome (Strutt 1779 & Caesar Commentaries): Cassivellaunus (54 BCE) → Cunobelinus → Caractacus & Queen Boadicea
sources: Joseph Strutt Chronicle of England (1779) p. 3
nodes.notes: Combines Caesar's eyewitness Commentaries (55-54 BCE) and Strutt's Chronicle of England: Cassivellaunus (commander against Julius Caesar) -> Tasciovanus -> Cunobelinus ('Cymbeline') -> Caractacus, alongside Iceni Queen Boadicea.

nodes.name: Venerable Bede's Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy (731 CE): Hengist & Horsa (from Woden) → King Ethelbert of Kent, Edwin & St. Oswald of Northumbria & Offa of Mercia
nodes.role: Germanic-Wodenic Kingdoms of the Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy
sources: Venerable Bede Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723 ed.)
nodes.notes: Bede explicitly traces Kentish brothers Hengist & Horsa (and fellow Heptarchy dynasties of Kent, Northumbria, Mercia, East Anglia & Wessex) to Woden -> Ethelbert of Kent (baptized 597), St. Edwin & St. Oswald of Northumbria, and Offa of Mercia.

nodes.name: Mézeray's First Race of France (1683): King Pharamond → Clodion → Meroveus (King III, Defeated Attila 451 CE) → Childeric I → Clovis I
nodes.role: Salian Frankish Founders of the First Race (Merovingians)
sources: François Eudes de Mézeray General Chronological History of France (1683) p. 10
nodes.notes: Mézeray (1683) documents the First Race of French monarchs from Pharamond and Clodion through Meroveus (King III, p. 10, who allied with Aëtius and Theodoric against Attila at the Catalaunian Plains, 451 CE), Childeric I, and Clovis I.

nodes.name: Sandford's Genealogical Proof of Portugal (1662): Robert Duke of Burgundy (Capetian Male Line) → Count Henry of Burgundy → Kings of Portugal
nodes.role: Strict Agnate Capetian Pedigree Refuting Alternative Legends for Count Henry
sources: Francis Sandford Genealogical History of the Kings of Portugal (1662) pp. 2-3
nodes.notes: Quoting Théodore Godefroy and ancient Fleury manuscripts (pp. 2-3), Sandford demonstrates Count Henry of Burgundy descended in direct male line from Robert the Pious & Robert I, Duke of Burgundy (House of France), marrying Alfonso VI's daughter Teresa in 1089/1090 to found Portugal's crown.
